chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muthanna from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"The Hajj is in well-known months": Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. It is not for anyone to enter into the state of Ihram for Hajj in any other than them, and it is not for anyone to enter into Ihram before the time that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated. And the example of that is the example of one who prays four [rak'ahs] during travel and leaves the two [rak'ahs]."

key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: To enter the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the specific months for Hajj and when can one enter Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal boundaries for entering *Ihram*, specifying Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah as the exclusive months for Hajj, thereby prohibiting premature commitment. The analogy to shortening prayers during travel underscores the principle of adhering strictly to divinely ordained limits, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding ritual precision. It reinforces the Prophetic tradition that the timing of Hajj is not arbitrary but fixed by the Messenger of Allah.
